about: The behavioural corpus for the bridge's PORT of the agent-board-toolkit's roster reader — which kanban user a coord roster says ONE seat is on ONE board instance (card#10868 Q1: the roster is the single store; card#10869: the bridge holds each agent's identity.kanban_user_id against it in `bridge:check`). The toolkit OWNS the rule. tests/Unit/Support/RosterKanbanUserParityTest.php runs every vector against the port on every test run; bin/kb-owner-parity.sh runs the same vectors through a toolkit checkout's own `kb_owner_resolve`.

authority.relationship: The toolkit OWNS this rule (README § "The card owner — the kanban assignee"). A disagreement is the bridge's defect to fix by re-porting, never the toolkit's to fix by matching the bridge.

how_the_far_end_runs_this: From a bridge checkout: `bin/kb-owner-parity.sh --corpus docs/kb-roster-uid-parity-corpus.json --toolkit <toolkit checkout>`. For each vector [config, seat, host] it writes `config` to a file — the string VERBATIM when `config` is a string (the file's exact text, used where a number literal must survive), else serialised and calls the toolkit's own `kb_owner_resolve` with COORD_CONFIG at that file, COORD_AGENT=seat and KB_API=https://<host>/api/v3. rc 0 must give KB_OWNER_USER_ID == expect.uid; rc 1 must give a KB_OWNER_WHY naming expect.why (absent: not a roster[].name; nofield: no `kanban_user_id` object; nohost: no entry for this board instance; bad: not a positive integer). A WHY the runner cannot classify is exit 2, never agreement. Exit 0 agreed, 1 drifted, 2 could not measure; `--control` perturbs every expectation and every pinned constant and must report each.
not_checked_by_this_repo: NOTHING IN THIS REPO'S CI RUNS THE TOOLKIT: a change to `kb_owner_resolve` or KB_JQ_ROSTER reds nothing here until someone runs bin/kb-owner-parity.sh against the changed toolkit. Run it on a toolkit bump.

The runner reads the authority's verdict through the WORDING of KB_OWNER_WHY (the function exposes no verdict code). A rewording it cannot classify is reported as could-not-measure (exit 2), so it fails loud rather than agreeing — but a rewording that moves one verdict's sentence onto another verdict's fragment would be misread.
`found` (the value that made a verdict `nofield`/`bad`) is bridge-local message detail and is not compared.

Whoever adds, changes or deletes a vector re-takes this measurement over the whole corpus: the bridge-side test reds on the digest until they do.

lookUp.why: PHP's json_decode gives `[]` and `{}` the same value, so the port cannot tell an empty LIST (authority: not the per-instance object, `nofield`) from an empty OBJECT (authority: `nohost`). Both verdicts mean the id is MISSING and both reach the same `warn`; only the verdict name in the message differs.

jq accepts any integral number at least 1; the port refuses a value that is not a JSON integer, and one larger than PHP_INT_MAX decodes to a float. The authority's answer is not a user id the board could hold either. The toolkit's integer-literal fix (card#10868 comment 7670) should converge this entry; the runner then reports it stale.

PHP's json_decode turns an OBJECT whose keys are "0".."n" into the same list an array decodes to, so the port reads such a roster as an array of seats; the toolkit's `roster | if type == "array"` reads it as no seats. The framework writes `roster` as an array; this shape is not one it produces.
